environmental_protection_agency_epa_envi.program_name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Environmental Justice Grants
environmental_protection_agency_epa_envi.description: Provides funding to community-based organizations working on environmental justice solutions to local environmental and public health issues in underserved communities. The program supports community-driven projects that address environmental and public health issues such as air quality, water quality, waste management, and climate resilience.
resident_input_opportunities: Required Public Hearings or Comment Periods: While specific requirements may vary, public input is crucial for community-driven projects. Applicants must ensure that community residents are integrally involved in project planning and execution.
Community Needs Assessment Processes: These processes are essential for identifying local environmental justice issues and developing strategies to address them.
Resident Advisory Committees or Councils: Encouraged to ensure ongoing community engagement and input.
Annual Planning or Reporting: Public input is typically required during annual planning processes to ensure that community priorities are reflected in project goals.
environmental_protection_agency_epa_envi.leverage_point: Influencing Local Funding Decisions: Residents can participate in public hearings and comment periods to influence project priorities. Participation in Planning Processes: Residents should engage early in project planning to ensure their concerns are addressed.

department_of_energy_doe_energy_efficien.program_name: Department of Energy (DOE) Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant
department_of_energy_doe_energy_efficien.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), specifically the Office of State and Community Energy Programs within the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
department_of_energy_doe_energy_efficien.description: The EECBG Program provides federal formula grants to local governments, states, and tribes to implement strategies that reduce energy use, lower fossil fuel emissions, and improve energy efficiency. Local governments play a central role by designing and executing projects that address community energy needs, sustainability, and climate action priorities[1][2][4].
eligible_activities: Developing and implementing local energy efficiency and conservation strategies[5].
Conducting energy audits and retrofits for residential and commercial buildings[1][5].
Establishing financial incentive programs (e.g., loans, rebates, permit fee waivers) for energy efficiency improvements[5].
Implementing renewable energy projects (e.g., solar or wind installations on public buildings)[4][5].
Developing and enforcing advanced building codes and inspection services to promote energy efficiency[1][5].
Supporting sustainable transportation initiatives (e.g., electric vehicle infrastructure, bike lanes, synchronized traffic signals)[4][5].
Programs addressing environmental justice and community engagement in energy planning[6].
resident_input_opportunities: Public hearings or comment periods: Many local governments hold public meetings or hearings to solicit feedback on proposed EECBG-funded projects and strategies[6].
Community needs assessments: Local governments often conduct assessments or surveys to identify community energy priorities, especially in environmental justice communities[6].
Resident advisory committees or councils: Some jurisdictions establish advisory groups to guide project selection and ensure diverse community representation[6].
Annual planning or reporting with public input: Local governments may be required to publish annual plans or reports and invite public comment before finalizing funding decisions[6].
department_of_energy_doe_energy_efficien.leverage_point: Participate in public meetings or hearings where EECBG strategies and projects are discussed. These are often announced on city or county websites and local media. Submit written comments during designated public comment periods, typically tied to annual planning or project proposal cycles.

clean_water_state_revolving_fund.administering_agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Water
clean_water_state_revolving_fund.description: Provides capitalization grants to states to establish revolving loan funds that provide low-cost financing for water quality infrastructure projects. CWSRF supports a wide range of projects including wastewater treatment facilities, stormwater management, green infrastructure, nonpoint source pollution control, and estuary protection. States have flexibility to set priorities and may offer additional subsidies for disadvantaged communities.
eligible_activities: Construction, repair, and rehabilitation of publicly owned wastewater treatment facilities
Combined sewer overflow (CSO) correction projects
Stormwater management and green infrastructure projects
Nonpoint source pollution control projects
Decentralized wastewater treatment systems
Water conservation and efficiency projects
Watershed protection and restoration projects
Lead service line replacement in certain circumstances
resident_input_opportunities: State CWSRF Intended Use Plan public hearings and comment periods
Local wastewater facility planning public meetings
Environmental review and permitting public comment opportunities
Disadvantaged community designation public input processes
clean_water_state_revolving_fund.leverage_point: Participate in state Intended Use Plan development to influence funding priorities. Engage with local government officials advocating for CWSRF-eligible projects. Support applications for projects addressing water quality in your community through public comment and attendance at planning meetings.

drinking_water_state_revolving_fund.administering_agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Water
drinking_water_state_revolving_fund.description: Provides capitalization grants to states for drinking water infrastructure improvements that facilitate compliance with Safe Drinking Water Act requirements and protect public health. DWSRF offers low-interest loans and additional subsidies to public water systems serving disadvantaged communities. The program addresses treatment upgrades, distribution system improvements, source water protection, and technical assistance for small systems.
eligible_activities: Installation, upgrade, and replacement of drinking water treatment facilities
Distribution system improvements including pipe replacement and storage tanks
Lead service line replacement and corrosion control
Source water protection and wellhead protection projects
Water system interconnections and consolidation
Technical assistance and operator training for small systems
Security improvements for drinking water facilities
Water meter installation and system monitoring equipment
resident_input_opportunities: State DWSRF Intended Use Plan public hearings and comment periods
Drinking water system capital improvement planning meetings
Consumer Confidence Report review and feedback opportunities
Public comment on water rate changes and system improvements
drinking_water_state_revolving_fund.leverage_point: Participate in state Intended Use Plan hearings to advocate for drinking water priorities. Engage with local water utilities on capital improvement plans. Review Consumer Confidence Reports and participate in rate-setting processes that fund local drinking water improvements.

brownfields_program.administering_agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Land and Emergency Management
brownfields_program.description: Provides grants and technical assistance to communities, states, tribes, and other stakeholders to assess, safely clean up, and sustainably reuse contaminated properties known as brownfields. The program supports environmental assessment, cleanup, job training, revolving loan funds, and technical assistance to address barriers to economic redevelopment posed by environmental contamination.
eligible_activities: Environmental site assessments (Phase I and Phase II) for brownfield properties
Cleanup of hazardous substances, pollutants, and contaminants
Petroleum cleanup at eligible underground storage tank sites
Establishment and operation of brownfield revolving loan funds
Job training for environmental careers in brownfield communities
Technical assistance for brownfield assessment and cleanup planning
Area-wide planning for brownfield redevelopment
Multipurpose grants combining assessment and cleanup activities
resident_input_opportunities: Brownfield grant application community involvement requirements
Site-specific cleanup planning public meetings
Area-wide planning community engagement processes
Environmental justice screening and community benefit discussions
brownfields_program.leverage_point: Participate in community engagement sessions during brownfield grant applications. Advocate for cleanup and redevelopment of specific contaminated sites. Engage with local government on brownfield inventory and prioritization. Provide input on desired end uses for cleaned-up properties.

clean_school_bus_program.administering_agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Transportation and Air Quality
clean_school_bus_program.description: Provides funding to replace existing school buses with zero-emission and low-emission models to reduce exposure to harmful air pollution for school children, bus drivers, and communities. Authorized under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, the program offers rebates and competitive grants to school districts, with priority for high-need local educational agencies, rural areas, and tribal schools.
eligible_activities: Replacement of existing diesel school buses with zero-emission electric buses
Replacement with low-emission alternative fuel buses (propane, CNG)
Purchase of charging infrastructure for electric school buses
Workforce training for electric bus maintenance and operation
Scrappage requirements for replaced diesel buses
resident_input_opportunities: School district budget and transportation planning meetings
School board meetings discussing fleet replacement applications
Parent-teacher organization discussions on student transportation
Community input on priority routes and equity considerations
clean_school_bus_program.leverage_point: Advocate at school board meetings for Clean School Bus Program applications. Engage with school district transportation departments on fleet electrification plans. Support applications by providing community input on air quality concerns and priority routes serving disadvantaged communities.
